turns.text: 9:40 pm update: theo finally did all three naps in the crib today. 9, 12:30 and 4, with 90-minute wake windows, no contact napping on me at all. scoreboard: dad 1, naps 3. i'd really like to protect this through the weekend. can you give me a plan to keep it consistent? in table form if possible, i think better in tables

Congratulations, three crib naps in one day is a real win. Here's a plan to protect it through the weekend.

| Time | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Wake-up | Feed, diaper, play | Note the exact wake time and count 90 minutes from it |
| ~8:30 | Start wind-down | Dim lights, sleep sack, white noise, same short phrase or song |
| ~9:00 | Nap 1 (crib) | Same room and same setup every time |
| ~10:30 | Wake, feed, play | Daylight and floor time |
| ~12:00 | Wind-down | Same routine, shorter |
| ~12:30 | Nap 2 (crib) | |
| ~2:00 | Wake, feed, play | Short outing or walk if you can |
| ~3:30 | Wind-down | |
| ~4:00 | Nap 3 (crib) | Cap it around 45-60 min so bedtime isn't pushed too far |

Weekend tips:
- Treat the wake windows as the anchor, not the clock. If he wakes early from a nap, adjust the next nap by the same amount.
- Keep the setup identical when other people are around: same crib, same sound, same wind-down.
- If you're out, a stroller or carrier nap is fine for one slot. Get back to the crib for the next one.
- Don't switch everything at once. Hold it for a few days before changing anything.

Want me to add the evening and bedtime piece?

yes please. the witching hour is the part i'm worried about, it runs roughly 5-8 and tonight was rough. how should bedtime fit after the 4 o'clock nap? also humming the slowed-down ballpark organ tune is what finally calmed him tonight. can i make that part of the routine or is that a bad idea

Humming the tune is a great idea. A consistent sound cue helps babies link it with winding down, and it's free and portable. Use it at the start of every nap wind-down and again at bedtime, so it means sleep rather than just rescue mode.

Here's how the evening can fit after a 4:00 nap:

| Time | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ~4:00-5:00 | Nap 3 | Wake him by 5:00 at the latest |
| ~5:00-6:30 | Witching hour, first half | Stroller walk, carrier, dim lights, hum the tune, avoid new stimulation |
| ~6:30-7:00 | Feed | A fuller feed here can help with the evening fussiness |
| ~7:00-7:30 | Bedtime routine | Bath or wipe-down, pajamas, sleep sack, white noise, tune |
| ~7:30-8:00 | Down for the night | Aim to put him down drowsy but awake |

Notes:
- With a 90-minute wake window, waking at 5:00 puts him ready for sleep around 6:30. Bedtime between 7:00 and 8:00 should fit the pattern.
- If the fussing runs past 8, a short soothing session with the tune is better than a long carry. You can then set him in the crib.
- Evening crying is common at this age and usually passes on its own. If it's intense, doesn't ease at all, or you're worried, call his pediatrician.
- Don't be discouraged if a day goes off-script. One bad evening doesn't undo the schedule.

Would you like a one-page checklist version you can keep on the fridge?
yes pls. also one thing, i need to answer that email during the 9 am nap tomorrow, so can you work that into the morning part so i don't skip the wind-down? typing one-handed sorry

No apology needed. Here's the fridge version with the email built in.

**Daily Crib Nap Checklist**

**Morning**
- [ ] Log the wake time and count 90 minutes
- [ ] ~8:30: Start wind-down (dim lights, sleep sack, white noise, hum the tune)
- [ ] ~9:00: Nap 1 in the crib
- [ ] ~9:05: Leave the room and open the email. Timebox it to 20-25 minutes, and set a phone timer so you're not tempted to stretch it
- [ ] ~10:30: He wakes, so feed and play

**Midday**
- [ ] ~12:00: Wind-down
- [ ] ~12:30: Nap 2 in the crib
- [ ] ~2:00: Wake, feed, outing or walk

**Afternoon/Evening**
- [ ] ~3:30: Wind-down
- [ ] ~4:00: Nap 3 in the crib, wake by 5:00
- [ ] 5:00-6:30: Witching hour tactics (walk, carrier, dim lights, hum the tune)
- [ ] ~6:30: Fuller feed
- [ ] ~7:00: Bedtime routine
- [ ] ~7:30-8:00: Down for the night

**Rules for the weekend**
- Anchor to wake windows, not the clock
- Same setup and cue every time
- One carrier or stroller nap is okay, then back to the crib

For the email, the nap is the time to write a short, clear reply. Draft the key points beforehand so it doesn't eat the whole nap. If you want, paste it here and I can help tighten it.
